description: The bytes at this entry are not valid code, so it is only a stub with no behaviour to describe.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the destination pointer passed on the stack is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the structure at the address register into it, then calls a routine through a register pointer.

name: prepare_command_buffer
description: Prepares a command buffer for an AmigaDOS command: it scans a linked list for its largest field value, reserves a longword array sized to match, fills it with a fixed pattern and a stack-frame pointer, then runs a 16-entry block copy. It returns zero on success and minus one when a step fails.

name: initialize_command_process
description: Program entry point for the Avail command: it allocates a record for the process, opens dos.library and raises an alert when that fails, parses the command line into argument strings that honour quotes and escape codes, then runs the command body and restores the saved state before returning.

name: finish_command_and_reply
description: Stores a result in the command record, closes the dos library, frees the record's buffers, replies to the waiting message, and returns that result.

name: sum_matching_memory_regions
description: Adds up a size difference for each memory region in a linked list whose attribute flags include the given mask, and returns the total.

name: print_memory_usage_table
description: Prints the memory usage report for the Avail command, showing the available, in-use, maximum and largest figures for chip, fast or total memory. It selects one memory type from the command argument when one is given.

name: call_with_stack_slot
description: Passes its two arguments to another routine together with a pointer to a stack slot that holds the third value.

name: call_global_and_checksum_buffer
description: Formats text into a 140-byte stack buffer through the exec formatting routine, computes an inverted count of the characters produced, and passes the buffer and count to another routine when the count is non-zero.
